messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — after flipping FP8-KV (fp8-kv-cuops-v2) on the small-prod pool we see decode jitter for short contexts. p50 up ~8-12ms for batch_size <= 3. Memory down ~17% but a small drop in nll for some prompts.
cheng: Copy. Any repro script/trace? Can you paste the profiler output?
zach: Seen similar on staging last week but assumed batch packing change. Can you confirm request size distribution?
maya: Request distro is mostly 1-3 tokens continued decode + short prompts (mean seq 24). Attached profiler snippet:
```
-- profiler summary (kv encode/decode hotspots) --
kernel: fp8-kv-cuops-v2 encode    p50 2.1ms p95 5.8ms
kernel: fp8-kv-cuops-v2 decode    p50 4.6ms p95 12.2ms
kernel: int8-kv-custom decode     p50 3.2ms p95 8.9ms
KV memory per-shard: fp8 1.1GB -> int8 1.4GB (but actual live mem reported lower due to packing)
batching: avg batch_size 1.8, max_batch_time_ms 8
```
maya: Also noticed occasional decode-quality blips — some token probability mass shifts on long-tail tokens vs baseline. Small but measurable in our smoke evals.
olivia: Did you use per-channel scale calibration or global? FP8 is sensitive. If we used a global scale it can mess up small activations.
maya: We ran the default --calib global method from the CI script. Command used: `./tools/kv_calib.py --model rwd-7b --dataset /data/kv-calib/samples.jsonl --format prefix --bits fp8 --method global --out /tmp/kv-calib`
cheng: Try `--method per-channel` and `--clip 3.0`, also run with `--hist-bins 2048`. FP8 layerwise scales helped us in the past for short-token patterns.
zach: Also check kernel selection fallback heuristics. If the runtime switches to fp8-kv-cuops-v2 for large batches but int8 for small, an incorrect hysteresis or decision threshold can flip often and add jitter. What does smart-routing/kernel-picker log show?
maya: kernel-picker shows quick toggles around seq_len=16 and batch_time=6ms. Logs: `picked fp8-kv-cuops-v2 for estimator_score 0.62 -> changed to int8-kv-custom after 7ms` repeated.
olivia: That screams hysteresis tuning. We should increase the dwell time and require >10% throughput improvement to switch. Also add a penalty for frequent flips.
cheng: For immediate mitigation: roll back fp8-kv to a canary subset (20% traffic) and force int8 for short-seq routes. Also re-run calib with per-channel scales and re-evaluate decode quality on our regression set.
zach: Agree. I can push a quick routing override: `route.policy.short_seq.force_kernel=int8-kv-custom` for pool small-prod.
infra-bot: deploy job rwd-kv-routing-1912345699 started by zach — canary 20% applied, rollback threshold p95+10ms.
maya: Thanks. After override p50 reverted to baseline within 5 minutes. I'll run the per-channel calib and post eval numbers here.
maya: (follow-up) Per-channel calib results: memory slightly worse (+4%) vs global but p50 stable and eval token-level delta reduced to ~0.05% negative. Command: `./tools/kv_calib.py --model rwd-7b --dataset /data/kv-calib/per_layer.jsonl --bits fp8 --method per-channel --clip 2.5 --out /tmp/kv-perlayer`
cheng: Great. Proposal: keep int8 for short-seq routing, fp8-per-channel for medium/long and tune kernel-picker to require 20ms dwell and 10% perf win to switch. Create a follow-up ticket to benchmark int4/mixed path for small-batch extreme memory cases.
maya: Filing ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/RWI-1023 — includes profiler dumps and calibration artifacts.
olivia: Nice writeup. Also add a short test in the perf harness: simulate lots of batch_size=1 decodes and assert p50 within X ms after kernel flip.
zach: I'll add the harness change.
maya: Closing for now — thanks everyone :thumbsup:
